skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian стол is a throne or chair); table and chair are obvious in English

examples.en: The film lasts two hours.
Old clocks hang on the wall.
We have six lessons tomorrow.

related.en: clock, watch — used only in the plural

examples.en: The bread is from yesterday, already stale.
The ice is still solid, you can go.
Have some strong tea.

related.en: hard, firm, solid — of ice, ground, a surface
strong, sturdy — of tea, sleep, health, a rope

examples.en: We have lunch at two o'clock.
At afternoon snack time the kids eat cookies.
There will be fish for dinner today.

related.en: afternoon snack — between lunch and dinner

note: Breakfast is «за́втрак».

examples.en: A black storm cloud hangs over the city.
There is not a single cloud in the sky.

related.en: storm cloud — a dark cloud full of rain or thunder

examples.en: I don't regret my decision.
He is always complaining about life.

related.en: to regret, to feel sorry for; to spare — «не жале́ть сил»

note: «Жале́ть» also means «to spare»: «не жале́ть сил» (to spare no effort).

examples.en: Give me a pen, I'll write it down.
Draw it with a pencil.

related.en: pen — a writing pen with ink; also a handle

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian гора is a forest); mountain and forest are obvious in English

examples.en: I was born in a big city.
It hailed in our neighborhood yesterday.

related.en: hail — ice falling from the clouds

note: The old word «град» (city) survives mostly in names: Белгра́д, Волгогра́д.

examples.en: I stopped by the store to get some bread.
She is reading a fashion magazine.

related.en: magazine — a periodical, also a journal

note: A false friend of English «magazine»: «магази́н» is a shop. It also means a gun magazine.

examples.ru: Его положили в [пала́ту] на втором этаже.
examples.en: He was put in a ward on the second floor.
Tourists are touring the tsar's palace.
The children are playing in the yard.

related.en: palace — a grand building of a ruler
yard, courtyard; also a royal court

examples.en: His cup of patience has overflowed.
Pour me a glass of water.
Drink a cup of tea while it's hot.

related.en: goblet, bowl — festive or figurative: «чаша терпения»
glass, tumbler — for water and juice, no handle

note: A shot glass is «рю́мка».

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian кућа is a house); pile versus home is not a real confusion for English speakers

examples.en: Tell me the whole truth.
I believe in justice.

note: In conversation «Пра́вда?» also means «Really?».

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian варење is digestion); jam versus digestion is not a confusion for English speakers

examples.en: On Saturdays we go to the bathhouse.
In summer they vacation at a resort.
There is no window in the bathroom.

related.en: bathhouse, Russian sauna — steamy, usually wooden
resort, spa — a place for vacation or treatment
bathroom — the room with the bath in an apartment

examples.en: A red squirrel lives in the park.
An egg has a yolk and a white.

note: The genitive of «бело́к» is «белка́», stressed on the end: «мно́го белка́» (a lot of protein).

examples.en: Our driver is very careful.
The show's new host cracks jokes all evening.

related.en: host, presenter — of a TV or radio show

examples.en: A coat of arms is shown on the coin.
A camel has two humps.

note: A hunchbacked person is «горба́тый».

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian зарез is a comma); the Russian заре́з exists only in the idiom «до заре́зу»
only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian застава is a flag); the Russian заста́ва is a rare word for a military post

examples.en: The witch was brewing a potion in a cauldron.
Add some fresh greens to the salad.

related.en: fresh herbs, greens — parsley, dill and the like

examples.en: She took a cookie with her coffee.
Mom made a roast for dinner.

related.en: roast — meat with vegetables cooked in an oven or pan

examples.en: We keep potatoes in the cellar.
The funeral will be on Friday.
The bicycle is in the basement.

related.en: cellar — an underground room for storing food
basement — the lower floor of a building

examples.en: The bank lowered the interest rate.
He placed a bet on his favorite team.
A new expense item has appeared in the budget.

related.en: article (in a paper); item (in a budget)

examples.en: A flock of ducks is flying over the lake.
The cow is standing in the cowshed.
The horse went back to the stable.

related.en: flock, pack — of birds, wolves, dogs: «во́лчья ста́я»
cowshed, pigsty — for cattle and pigs

examples.en: Don't touch the wire, it's live!
The current carried the boat away.

examples.ru: В [тече́ние] недели я буду в отъезде.
examples.en: I'll be away this week.

related.en: current, flow of water; «в тече́ние» means «during, over the course of»

examples.ru: У нас с тобой есть общее [де́ло].
examples.en: You and I have a cause in common.
This work was written in the nineteenth century.

related.en: a work — of literature, art or music

note: «Как дела́?» means «How are things?».

examples.en: Don't ask me about that.
He is trying to open the window.
I eat at home.

related.en: to eat, to feed oneself — «питаться до́ма»

note: «Пыта́ть» without «-ся» means «to torture».

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian брод is a ship); the Russian брод is just a ford

examples.en: My favorite color is blue.
She gave me a flower.

note: The plural «цветы́» means flowers, «цвета́» means colors.

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian воз is a train); the Russian воз is a rare word for a cartload

examples.en: Documents must be kept in a safe.

examples.ru: Мама [ко́рмит] кота два раза в день.
examples.en: Mom feeds the cat twice a day.

related.en: to keep, to store — in a safe place
to feed — a child, an animal

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian губа is leprosy); lip and mouth are obvious in English

examples.en: Flour is needed for blini.
Waiting is agony.

note: Two different words spelled the same, told apart only by stress: «мука́» (flour) and «му́ка» (torment, pl. «му́ки»).

examples.en: The fridge is completely empty.
Don't ask idle questions.

note: «Пра́здный» is bookish: «пра́здное любопы́тство» (idle curiosity).

examples.en: A rainbow appeared after the rain.
An electric arc dazzles the eyes.

related.en: arc, curve — an electric arc, the bow of a horse's harness

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian лопта is a ball); shovel and ball are obvious in English

examples.en: He never forgave her betrayal.
The schedule has changed.

note: The verb «измени́ть» means both «to change» (+ acc.) and «to betray, be unfaithful to» (+ dat.).

examples.en: He is too stingy to leave a tip.
This coat is too expensive.

note: «Дорого́й» also means «dear»: «дорого́й друг».

examples.en: The money goes into the treasury.
They abolished the death penalty in that country.
What punishment did he get?

note: A fine is «штраф»; the death penalty is «сме́ртная казнь».

examples.en: I have a headache.
I read the first chapter of the book.

note: «Глава́ семьи́» means «head of the family».

skip: only a Serbian false-friend trap (Serbian стан is an apartment); the Russian стан is a rare bookish word

examples.ru: Ночью стало холодно, и я взял второе [одея́ло].
examples.en: It got cold at night, so I took a second blanket.
I wear these clothes at home.

related.en: clothes, clothing — a collective noun, no plural

examples.en: He likes catching fish.
In his youth my grandfather hunted wild boar.

note: «Лови́ть» means to catch: «лови́ть ры́бу», «лови́ть мяч». A hunter is «охо́тник».

examples.en: I'm learning the words for the exam.
My sister studies at the university.
He is studying art history.
In the evenings I study English.

related.en: to learn something; to teach someone — «учи́ть слова́», «учи́ть ребёнка»
to study, to be a student — «он у́чится в шко́ле»
to work on something, to do — «занима́ться спо́ртом»

note: «Учи́ть» takes an object: «учи́ть слова́», «учи́ть ребёнка». Without an object, or with an infinitive, use «учи́ться»: «он у́чится в шко́ле», «она́ у́чится води́ть» (she is learning to drive).

examples.en: Do you know his phone number?
My daughter can read.
I can't come tomorrow.

related.en: to know — a fact, a person, an answer: «зна́ть отве́т»
to know how to, can — a learned skill
can, to be able to — possibility or permission

note: For a learned skill use «уме́ть»: «я уме́ю пла́вать» (I can swim), not «я зна́ю пла́вать». «Зна́ть» is not used with an infinitive.

examples.en: I always put my keys in my pocket.
Put the book on the table.
You are putting the bottle on the shelf.
We are hanging the picture on the wall.

related.en: to put, to lay — so that it lies flat: «кла́сть кни́гу на стол»
to put, to lay (pf. of «кла́сть») — «положи́ть телефо́н на стол»
to put, to stand — upright: «ста́вить ча́шку, буты́лку»

note: Where English says «put», Russian picks a verb by the position of the object: lying (кла́сть), standing (ста́вить) or hanging (ве́шать).

examples.en: I like listening to music.
Do you hear that noise?

note: «Слу́шать» is on purpose, «слы́шать» is by chance: «Я слы́шал, что...» (I heard that...), «слу́шай меня́» (listen to me).

examples.en: In the evening we watch a movie.
I can't see without glasses.

note: «Смотри́ на меня́» means «look at me», «я тебя́ ви́жу» means «I see you».

examples.en: He speaks English well.
He said he would come.
We talked on the phone for a long time.

related.en: to speak, to talk — a language or an ongoing action: «говори́ть по-ру́сски»
to say, to tell (pf.) — one statement
to talk, to have a conversation — «разгова́ривать по телефо́ну»

note: A language is always «spoken» with «говори́ть»: «говори́ть по-ру́сски». «Сказа́ть» is perfective: «он сказа́л, что...» (he said that...).

examples.en: The child asks where Mom is.
She asks me to help her.

related.en: to ask, to request — that someone do something: «проси́ть о по́мощи»

note: «Спра́шивать» asks for information. To ask someone to do something, use «проси́ть»: «попроси́ его́ помо́чь» (ask him to help).

examples.en: I always take an umbrella with me.
Take my pen.

related.en: to take (impf.) — repeated or ongoing: «брать с собо́й»

note: «Брать» is imperfective, «взять» perfective: «возьми́ ключи́» (take the keys, once), «всегда́ бери́ ключи́» (always take the keys).

examples.en: Are you going? So am I.
He knows English, and German as well.

related.en: also, as well — adds to a list, more formal

note: «То́же» means «me too, he too»: «я то́же люблю́ ко́фе». «Та́кже» just adds: «я люблю́ ко́фе, а та́кже чай».

examples.en: He is still asleep.
We are already home.

note: «Ещё не» means «not yet», «уже́ не» means «no longer»: «он ещё не пришёл» (he hasn't come yet), «его́ уже́ нет» (he is no longer here).

examples.en: I can't talk right now.

examples.ru: Раньше он жил в Москве, а [тепе́рь] живёт в Казани.
examples.en: He used to live in Moscow, and now he lives in Kazan.

related.en: now, right now; also «in a moment»
now, from now on — in contrast to before

note: «Я сейча́с приду́» means «I'll be right there». «Тепе́рь» always implies a change: it was different before, now it is like this.

examples.en: He worked all day.
I ate a whole watermelon.

related.en: all, the whole — everything of a known whole: «весь го́род»
whole, entire — a complete piece or a large amount: «це́лый час»; also intact

note: «Весь/вся/всё/все» means all of a known whole: «вся семья́». «Це́лый» stresses a complete piece or amount: «це́лая пи́цца», «це́лый час». It also means intact: «це́лая ча́шка».

examples.en: Where do you live?
Where are you going?

related.en: where — the place where someone or something is
where to — the direction of movement

note: With verbs of motion use «куда́», not «где»: «куда́ ты идёшь?». «Отку́да» means «from where».

examples.en: I'm here, waiting for you.
Come here and have a look!
My friends live there.
We are going there by train.

note: Russian has separate words for motion: «иди́ сюда́» (come here), «я е́ду туда́» (I'm going there). «Здесь» and «там» are for being in a place.

examples.en: I have to go.
You need to rest.

related.en: need to, have to — colloquial, the person in the dative: «мне на́до идти́»
necessary, need — somewhat stricter; the adjective «ну́жный» means «needed»

note: Both take the dative and an infinitive. For a thing that is needed, «ну́жный» is usual: «мне нужна́ ва́ша по́мощь» (I need your help).
